verdict.rationale: The CLI documents `skills init [name]` to "Create a new SKILL.md template", and the linked Agent Skills specification says SKILL.md must carry YAML frontmatter, with agents loading each skill's name and description at startup. However, no evidence shows what the generated template contains, so the name/description frontmatter in the scaffold is only implied. missing for 10: documentation or a hands-on sample of the `skills init` output showing name and description frontmatter fields, an explicit spec table defining the required name/description fields, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the authoring flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can author a new skill from a documented template — a SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter — without reverse-engineering existing skills

citations.quote: `skills init [name]` | Create a new SKILL.md template
The SKILL.md file must contain YAML frontmatter followed by Markdown content.
At startup, agents load only the name and description of each available skill, just enough to know when it might be relevant.
